messages.subject: "slm" random effect
parts:
Hi. I have a data set, if I only want to model part of the data as a spatial error model, is that OK? How to use "slm" potential effects to achieve? I operate as follows: suppose there are m rows in the data set, and I want to build a spatial error model for n rows of data. The id of the inner part of the spatial error model is n, and the id of the remaining M-N rows is NA. The code is written like this:

sem<-inla( y ~ 1 + x +
               f(idx, model="slm", args.slm=list(rho.min = rho.min ,rho.max = rho.max, W = w, X =                                                                    matrix(0, nrow(Ndata), 0), Q.beta = matrix(1, 0, 0)), 
                                                 hyper.slm=hyper.slm),
              data=Mdata, family="poisson",E=E)

    •   I want to know why writing code like this causes errors, and how can I correct it? Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "slm" random effect
parts:
you can also use the slm model in a joint model, but you have to be
careful as the 'slm' model is using a fake likelihood to achive it.
please refer to one of the (free-)books on r-inla.org for how to setup
joint models (or models with more than one likelihood)

Best
H
